clinicalPearls: Galactosialidosis is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by CTSA variants, resulting in deficiency of protective protein/cathepsin A
The deficient cathepsin A normally stabilises a complex with beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase, so its loss produces a combined deficiency of both enzymes
Three clinical forms are recognised by age at onset: early-infantile, late-infantile, and juvenile/adult, the last being commoner in patients of Japanese ancestry
Characteristic features include coarse facial features, a macular cherry-red spot, dysostosis multiplex, and, in the early-infantile form, hydrops fetalis and visceromegaly
The juvenile/adult form is dominated by progressive neurological decline with myoclonus, ataxia, cognitive impairment, and angiokeratoma of the skin
Diagnosis is supported by increased urinary sialylated oligosaccharides and confirmed by combined beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase deficiency with CTSA genetic testing
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary, as no specific disease-modifying therapy is established
reference.pathophysiology: Cathepsin A (protective protein) forms a lysosomal multienzyme complex with beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase (sialidase), protecting them from premature degradation and enabling their normal activity. In galactosialidosis, biallelic CTSA variants cause loss of this protective function, leading to a secondary combined deficiency of both beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase. Impaired degradation results in lysosomal accumulation of sialylated glycoproteins, oligosaccharides, and glycolipids in neurones and visceral tissues. This storage underlies the neurodegeneration, cherry-red spot, coarse features, skeletal dysostosis, and, in severe forms, the fetal hydrops and organomegaly.
additionalDifferentials: Other lysosomal causes of a cherry-red spot (e.g. Tay-Sachs, Niemann-Pick)
Other progressive myoclonic epilepsies in the juvenile/adult form
Non-immune hydrops fetalis of other lysosomal or metabolic cause
additionalInvestigations: Urinary oligosaccharide analysis showing increased sialylated oligosaccharides
Enzyme assays demonstrating combined deficiency of beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase
Ophthalmological examination for a macular cherry-red spot
Skeletal survey for dysostosis multiplex and brain MRI to assess atrophy and white-matter change
redFlags: Non-immune hydrops fetalis or severe visceromegaly in the early-infantile form
Rapid neurological regression with intractable myoclonus
Progressive visual loss associated with the cherry-red spot
Cardiac or renal involvement contributing to deterioration
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the form: the early-infantile type is severe and often fatal in infancy, the late-infantile type is intermediate, and the juvenile/adult type is slowly progressive with prolonged survival but accumulating neurological disability.
pitfalls: Diagnosing isolated sialidosis or GM1 gangliosidosis and missing the combined deficiency of galactosialidosis
Overlooking galactosialidosis as a cause of non-immune hydrops fetalis
Failing to consider it in a juvenile/adult progressive myoclonic epilepsy with a cherry-red spot
Not recognising the ancestry-related frequency of the juvenile/adult form
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: No disease-specific enzyme or curative therapy is available, so management is supportive and symptom-directed
Antimyoclonic and antiseizure medications for the myoclonus and seizures of the juvenile and adult forms
Physiotherapy, occupational therapy and mobility aids for the progressive ataxia and neurological decline
Nutritional support and management of feeding difficulties, with assisted feeding as the disease progresses
In the early-infantile form, supportive management of hydrops foetalis, visceromegaly and organ dysfunction
Surveillance with ophthalmological review for the cherry-red spot, skeletal and neuroimaging monitoring, and developmental assessment
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance with family screening and offer of prenatal testing
Multidisciplinary and palliative care involving metabolic medicine, neurology and clinical genetics
